title: Prompt Warrior - A dungeon exploration game
author: HrodRuck
selftext:
In this game, you control your character by typing what you want to do. The mechanics are also written in natural language, making extension (new dungeon rooms) really easy and fun.

  
What I have now is [a simple 3-room experience](https://prompt-warrior-1.onrender.com/). I would appreciate feedback, especially regarding the mechanics and what stops/enables the fun for you. I'm also open for questions. Thanks!

comments.author: Spamshazzam
comments.body: I just found this and I'm playing it now. I'll come back in a bit with some specific improvement feedback, but I'm enjoying it a lot.

replies.author: HrodRuck
replies.body: That's great to hear! Did you manage to beat the dungeon?

replies.author: Spamshazzam
replies.body:
I did! I played through several times actually, and sandboxed one of the runs, trying to game the system. I have bunch of notes I can give you when I have a chance to type it up.

Do you have some details you can share about the type of game it's meant to be, or the vibe you want it to have? Knowing will help me know what feedback is helpful.

replies.author: HrodRuck
replies.body:
Sorry for the delay! I'm not a frequent user of reddit and ended up losing your message for a while. Hope you had fun!!  


The vision I have for this is that people can make their own little dungeons using only natural language and share with their friends. Since the game mechanics are also written as prompts under the hood. The next step would be exposing this capability in a kind of level editor where you edit not only the map, but any of the rules as well.  
For example, one could make a nature-themed dungeon where play as a druid and lose power for 3 turns "if you mistreat an animal". And let the engine deal with that ambiguity.

  
But idk, maybe you have even better ideas than me! haha. Feedback is VERY welcome.

replies.author: HrodRuck
